_meta.title: Household solar + battery cost, performance and finance assumptions (California, 2026)
notes: kind 'assumption' marks a Griddy choice, with the reason in note.
All $ are nominal unless noted. NPV discounts nominal cash flows at discount_rate_pct.

pv_installed_usd_per_w.source: LBNL, U.S. Distributed Solar and Storage: 2025 Data Update (Oct 2025), slide 38 'State-Level Differences in Installed Prices'
pv_installed_usd_per_w.note: Slide 38 bar chart, 'Residential Systems Installed in 2024, Median Installed Price and 20th/80th Percentiles (2024$/W_DC)', host-owned stand-alone residential PV: CA = $4.0. Slide 8: 'loan-financed systems were considerably higher priced than cash-purchase systems in 2024 (median prices of $4.7/W vs. $3.5/W)' (national). Prices are 'the gross price paid by the system owner, before any incentives or tax credits'.

pv_plus_storage_premium_usd_per_w.units: USD per W of PV capacity (2024$), cash purchase
pv_plus_storage_premium_usd_per_w.source: LBNL, U.S. Distributed Solar and Storage: 2025 Data Update, slide 9
pv_plus_storage_premium_usd_per_w.note: 'The median cash price of paired residential systems in 2024 was $1.7/W higher than for stand-alone systems' ($5.3/W vs $3.5/W cash; ~90% of the paired residential pricing data is from California). Slide 7: 'Residential battery storage systems had a median size of 13.5 kWh in 2024'. Cross-check only.

battery_installed_usd_per_kwh.units: USD per kWh of storage capacity, installed, before incentives
battery_installed_usd_per_kwh.source: EnergySage, Cost of Energy Storage in California (marketplace quote data, updated Oct 18, 2026)
battery_installed_usd_per_kwh.note: 'As of October 2026, the average storage system cost in California is $1,037/kWh'; 'an average storage installation in California ranges in cost from $11,460 to $15,504' for a 13 kWh system. Marketplace quotes, not a government survey. Cross-check (inferred): LBNL's $1.7/W paired premium x 5.7 kW (slide 4: CA 'had a relatively small median size of 5.7 kW') / 13.5 kWh is about $718/kWh, which is lower because it is a premium added to a solar install.

federal_residential_clean_energy_credit_.units: percent of eligible cost, for systems installed in 2026
federal_residential_clean_energy_credit_.source: IRS, Residential Clean Energy Credit (26 U.S.C. 25D) page, last reviewed or updated 04-Jul-2026
federal_residential_clean_energy_credit_.note: IRS: 'The credit is not available for any property placed in service after December 31, 2025.' Before that it 'equals 30% of the costs of new, qualified clean energy property' (2022-2025), including 'Battery storage technology (beginning in 2023)' of at least 3 kWh. Griddy applies 0% to 2026 homeowner-owned installs. Leases/PPAs (third-party owned) fall under business credits and are not modelled (UNCONFIRMED).

battery_round_trip_efficiency.source: NREL/NLR Annual Technology Baseline 2025, Residential Battery Storage
battery_round_trip_efficiency.note: ATB 2025: Cole et al. 'identified 85% as a representative roundtrip efficiency' and the 2025 ATB 'adopts this value'. Representative system 'a 5-kilowatt (kW)/12.5-kilowatt hour (kWh; 2.5-hour) system'.

battery_life_years.source: NREL/NLR Annual Technology Baseline 2025, Residential Battery Storage
battery_life_years.note: ATB 2025 O&M section: the system is operated 'throughout its 15-year lifetime'. Griddy does not add a replacement inside a 25-year NPV (assumption; say so).

pv_degradation_pct_per_yr.source: Jordan & Kurtz, 'Photovoltaic Degradation Rates: An Analytical Review', NREL/JA-5200-51664 (2012)
pv_degradation_pct_per_yr.note: Abstract: 'Nearly 2000 degradation rates, measured on individual modules or entire systems, have been assembled from the literature, showing a median value of 0.5%/year.' The ATB 2025 residential PV page uses 'an assumed degradation rate of 0.7%/yr' (https://atb.nlr.gov/electricity/2025/residential_pv) for a more conservative case.

pv_system_life_years.source: Griddy assumption (Griddy Home spec: NPV over 25 years)
pv_system_life_years.note: Griddy runs NPV over 25 years. The ATB 2025 residential PV page models capacity factors 'over the 30-year lifetime of the system', so 25 is the conservative choice. Inverter replacement is not modelled.

rate_escalation_pct_per_yr.source: EIA State Electricity Profile, California, Table 8 (Form EIA-861), residential average price 1990-2024
rate_escalation_pct_per_yr.note: Default = 20-year compound growth of the CA residential average price, 12.20 cents/kWh (2004) -> 31.97 cents/kWh (2024): (31.97/12.20)^(1/20)-1 = 4.93%/yr. The more recent windows run hotter: 10-yr 16.25 (2014) -> 31.97 = 7.00%/yr; 5-yr 19.15 (2019) -> 31.97 = 10.79%/yr. PG&E residential rates were cut in March and June 2026 (tariff sheets marked (R)), so Griddy defaults to the long-run figure. The user can change it.

discount_rate_pct.note: Nominal rate for discounting household cash flows. Bills are escalated in nominal terms, so the rate is nominal too. Roughly a homeowner's opportunity cost of cash or a home-equity loan rate; not taken from a published source. User-visible and adjustable.
